To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the gauge invariance issue of angular momentum in QED and QCD can be resolved, and 2) the gauge-invariant definition of the angular momentum in QCD is the same as that in QED, except for the replacement of $\vec E$ and $\vec B$ by the gluon field strength tensor $F^a_{\mu\nu}$, where the gauge index $a$ runs over the color indices.

the spin and orbital angular momentum of electrons and photons in QED can be consistently defined gauge-invariantly, and that the canonical operators $\psi ^\dag \vec x \psi$, $\psi ^\ast \vec x\times\frac 1 i \vec \n abla\psi$ are gauge-invariant quantities.

the spin and orbital angular momentum of a charged particle in a gauge theory is the sum of its spin and the angular momentum of its gauge-field interaction, that the gauge-field interaction angular momentum is determined by the gauge field's canonical angular-momentum density, and that the canonical angular-momentum densities of a charged particle and its gauge field are not equal to the angular-momentum densities in the standard textbook formulas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions in quantum electrodynamics (QED): (i) Can the spin and orbital angular momentum of the electron be consistently defined in the presence of gauge fields?
the angular-momentum flow of gauge theories and its connection to the spin structure of matter.
the gauge-invariant definition of angular momentum, its density, and its conservation laws.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gauge-invariant angular momentum in gauge theory has been found, and that the canonical angular momentum is the correct gauge-invariant one.
the spin and orbital angular-momentum densities of electrons and photons, and of quarks and gluons in QCD, can all be consistently and unambiguously defined gauge-invariantly.
the gauge invariance issue of angular momentum has been settled in gauge theories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a gauge invariant, consistent, and complete theory of angular momentum in quantum electrodynamics, and the same can also be applied to non-Abelain gauge theories.

we have found an effective way to define and compute the angular momentum of a gauge field, and thus the total angular momentum of a system of charged particles and gauge field, without the need of gauge fixing.
we have finally resolved the gauge invariance puzzle of angular momentum in physics, which has been haunting people for more than half a century.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in a gauge-invariant formulation, the gauge-invariant angular momentum density can be consistently defined, computed, and interpreted in terms of the canonical, gauge-invariant operators, and is in fact what one does in atomic physics.
the angular momentum of gauge fields can be consistently defined in the Coulomb (or other gauges), which has been a long-standing problem in gauge theories.
the gauge invariance issue is a red herring.
